title: Virginia Jury Finds Naresh Bhatt Guilty of Murdering Wife Mamta Kafle Bhatt
excerpt: A Prince William County jury convicted Bhatt of first-degree murder and of concealing and defiling a dead body, rejecting his testimony that his wife died by suicide and he only disposed of her body.
body:
• A Prince William County, Virginia jury on Tuesday found Naresh Bhatt, 39, guilty of first-degree murder in the death of his wife, Mamta Kafle Bhatt, 28, plus concealing and defiling a dead body.
  • Bhatt testified that he found his wife dead by suicide on July 30, 2024, panicked, and dismembered and disposed of her body; he denied killing her. The jury rejected that account after about four hours of deliberation, according to FOX 5 DC.
  • Mamta Kafle Bhatt, a registered nurse last seen on July 27, 2024, at UVA Health Prince William Medical Center in Manassas, has never been found.
  • Bhatt faces up to life in prison for first-degree murder plus up to five years on each of the other two charges; sentencing is set for March 12, 2027, and his bond was revoked.

A Virginia jury has found Naresh Bhatt guilty of first-degree murder in the death of his wife, Mamta Kafle Bhatt, rejecting his testimony that she died by suicide and that he only dismembered and disposed of her body afterward.

According to CNN, jurors on Tuesday also convicted Bhatt, 39, of concealing and defiling his wife's body. FOX 5 DC reported the jury deliberated for four hours before delivering the guilty verdict, at the end of a six-week trial. The case was heard in Prince William County; CNN quoted a statement from Amy Ashworth, the commonwealth's attorney for Prince William County and the Cities of Manassas and Manassas Park.

"This verdict represents an important measure of justice for Mamta Kafle Bhatt, whose life was tragically taken and whose family has endured more than two years of unimaginable pain and uncertainty."

— Amy Ashworth, Commonwealth's Attorney for Prince William County, in a statement reported by CNN

What Bhatt admitted — and what he denied

Bhatt took the witness stand in his own defense. He testified that he woke in the middle of the night and found Kafle Bhatt unconscious, surrounded by vomit and blood in their bedroom, tried to resuscitate her for about an hour, and did not call 911, according to CNN's account of reporting by WUSA. He said he then concealed her body, put her remains in multiple trash bags, and threw them into a trash compactor at an apartment complex where he used to live, and that he took his then-11-month-old child on some of those trips. FOX 5 DC reported he testified he found his wife dead from suicide in their bedroom on July 30, 2024, and dismembered her body inside their home before disposing of her remains. He denied killing her throughout.

The disappearance

Kafle Bhatt was last seen on July 27, 2024, at UVA Health Prince William Medical Center in Manassas, Virginia, where the 28-year-old mother worked as a registered nurse, according to police as reported by CNN. The next day, a friend spoke with her by phone and she posted a video of herself and her infant daughter on TikTok, CNN reported, citing affiliate WJLA. Her body has never been found. When she disappeared, Bhatt told police and media he last saw her at their dinner table several days before he reported her missing, CNN reported.

After the verdict, Holly Wirth, a close friend and former colleague, thanked prosecutors and law enforcement outside court, CNN reported. Sunita Basnet, another friend and colleague, said more work needs to be done in the community regarding domestic violence.

Sentencing and appeal

Bhatt could be sentenced to up to life in prison for first-degree murder, plus an additional five years for each of the concealing and defiling charges, CNN reported. FOX 5 DC reported that Bhatt is scheduled for a sentencing hearing on March 12, 2027, where he could face life in prison. CNN reported Bhatt is expected to be sentenced March 12 and that the judge revoked his bond. FOX 5 DC reported that Virginia law grants Bhatt an automatic right of appeal to the Virginia Court of Appeals, and quoted trial attorney Mike Hollingsworth — who was not involved in the case — assessing the defense's position after Bhatt's admissions on the stand. Bhatt's own attorney told CNN they were unable to comment before the case concludes.
nri_angle: The verdict closes a two-year case followed closely in Northern Virginia and in Nepal, where Mamta Kafle Bhatt's family campaigned for answers after her 2024 disappearance.
